'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Battle of Geneina]]
***More than 1,000 bodies are discovered in 30 [[mass grave]]s within the [[Rapid Support Forces|RSF]]-occupied city of [[Geneina]] in [[West Darfur]], [[Sudan]], by civil leaders. [https://www.dabangasudan.org/en/all-news/article/more-mass-graves-found-in-west-darfur-rsf-accused-of-demolishing-camps (Radio Dabanga)]
**[[Sudanese refugee crisis]]
***The number of [[refugee|people who have fled]] Sudan since April reaches 1 million while nearly 3.5 million have been [[internally displaced]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/situation-sudan-spiralling-out-control-after-four-months-war-un-2023-08-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Islamist insurgency in the Sahel]]
**[[Jihadist insurgency in Niger]]
***Seventeen [[Niger Armed Forces|soldiers]] are killed and 20 others are injured in an [[ambush]] of a [[military vehicle]] in Koutougou, [[Tillabéri Region]], [[Niger]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/8/16/more-than-a-dozen-niger-troops-killed-in-attack-near-mali-border (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Libyan Crisis (2011–present)|Libyan Crisis]]
**[[2023 Tripoli clashes]]
***The death toll from fighting in [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]] between the 444 brigade and the [[RADA Special Deterrence Forces|Special Deterrence Force]] increases to 55 people, with 146 more injured. The fighting ends following the release of a commander. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/8/16/libya-fighting-leaves-dead-dozens-injured-medics (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[2022–2023 western Russia attacks]]
***[[government of Russia|Russia]]'s [[Federal Security Service]] says that it has stopped a [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[sabotage]] group, consisting of four fighters, from infiltrating [[Russia–Ukraine border|the border]] in [[Starodubsky District]], [[Bryansk Oblast]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2023/08/16/Russia-s-FSB-foils-attempt-by-Ukrainian-saboteurs-to-cross-into-Bryansk-four-killed (AFP via Al Arabiya)]
**[[2023 Ukrainian counteroffensive]]
***Ukraine recaptures the village of [[Urozhaine, Donetsk Oblast|Urozhaine]], [[Donetsk Oblast]], from [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2023/08/16/europe/urozhaine-donetsk-ukraine-reclaims-intl/index.html (CNN)]
**A [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] strike in [[Dnipropetrovsk Oblast]] kills a [[civilian]] and injures six others, and damaging agriculture and civilian infrastructure. [https://edition.cnn.com/europe/live-news/russia-ukraine-war-news-08-16-23/h_8675af5817308ed872503a1bc6a2f89f (CNN International)]
*A [[Islam in Pakistan|Muslim]] mob storms a [[Christianity in Pakistan|Christian]] area in [[Jaranwala]], [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab]], [[Pakistan]], burning a church, damaging two other churches, and demolishing the house of a man who they accused of [[Quran desecration|desecrating]] the pages of a [[Quran]]. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-muslim-attack-churches-blasphemy-christian-faisalabad-bc671037bdd389af6b67e0292cc18582 (AP)]
'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**The [[Ship registration in Hong Kong|Hong Kong-flagged]] ''Joseph Schulte'' becomes the first [[cargo ship]] to depart from the [[Port of Odesa]], [[Ukraine]]'s largest [[seaport]], using new [[Black Sea]] [[shipping lane]]s, after [[Russia]] withdrew from the [[Black Sea Grain Initiative]]. [https://mb.com.ph/2023/8/16/ukraine-says-first-cargo-ship-exits-black-sea-port-via-new-corridor (AFP via ''Manila Bulletin'')]
*[[Economy of the Netherlands]]
**The [[Netherlands]] [[Statistics Netherlands|statistics office]] reports that the country has entered a [[recession]] after the economy declined by 0.3% in the second quarter with [[exports]] and household spending falling despite rising [[interest rates]] that were intended to lower [[inflation]]. [https://apnews.com/article/netherlands-recession-economy-interest-rates-inflation-trade-c05e6a7abd2c9e950a26fc6cac5e6278 (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2023 Cape Verde migrant boat disaster]]
**At least 63 people are killed and 38 others are rescued after a boat carrying mostly Senegalese migrants [[capsize]]s off the coast of [[Cape Verde]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/8/16/dozens-feared-dead-after-boat-capsizes-off-cape-verde (Al Jazeera)] 
*[[2023 Hawaii wildfires]]
**The [[Hawaii Route 30#Related route|Lahaina Bypass]] in west [[Maui]], [[Hawaii]], [[United States]], reopens to traffic after being closed for a week due to the [[wildfire|wildfires]]. [https://www.khon2.com/hawaii-fires/lahaina-bypass-now-open-to-everyone/amp/ (KHON-TV)]
*[[2023 Hpakant jade mine disaster]]
**The death toll from the 13 August [[landslide]] at a [[jade trade in Myanmar|jade mine]] in [[Hpakant]], [[Kachin State|Kachin]], [[Myanmar]], increases to 31, with eight people still missing. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/world/2630539 (AFP via ''Bangkok Post'')]
*The death toll from the [[explosion]] in [[San Cristóbal, Dominican Republic|San Cristóbal]], [[Dominican Republic]], on 14 August increases to 27, after sixteen more people are found dead. The cause is still unknown. [https://apnews.com/article/dominican-republic-explosion-dead-missing-cc1b8f3ae5e1bb0c64d80db1fd096ba1 (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*Surgeons from [[NYU Langone Health]] in the United States report the successful functioning of a [[Genetically modified animal|genetically modified]] pig [[Kidney transplantation|kidney in a human recipient]] for 32 days, a record in [[xenotransplantation]]. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2023/08/17/world/science-health/us-pig-kidney-human/ (AFP via ''The Japan Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[North Korea–United States relations]]
**The [[Korean Central News Agency]] confirms that [[United States Army]] soldier [[Travis King]] has been detained for [[illegal entry]], stating that King claimed "inhuman maltreatment and racial discrimination" within the [[United States Army|U.S. Army]] and also that he is seeking [[refugee]] status in the country. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/north-korea-says-us-soldier-travis-king-expressed-willingness-seek-refuge-kcna-2023-08-15/ (Reuters)]
*A lawsuit is filed against the [[Hawaiian Electric Industries]] company, accusing it of negligence as the reason for the wildfires. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/antoniopequenoiv/2023/08/16/hawaiian-electric-accused-of-inaction-causing-maui-wildfire-disaster-in-negligence-lawsuit/amp/ (''Forbes'')]
*[[Singapore Police Force|Singapore police]] arrest ten foreign nationals and [[Asset forfeiture|seize assets]] worth approximately [[Singapore dollar|S$]]1 billion ([[United States dollar|US$]]750 million), suspecting involvement in an international [[money laundering]] operation tied to [[transnational organized crime]], including [[online gambling]] and [[Internet fraud]]. [https://guardian.ng/news/singapore-seizes-736-million-in-assets-in-anti-laundering-raids/ (AFP via ''The Guardian'')]
*[[Spanish Civil Guard]] police arrest five [[French people|French]] tourists and one [[Swiss people|Swiss]] tourist for allegedly [[raping]] an 18-year-old [[British people|British]] woman on the island of [[Mallorca]]. [https://apnews.com/article/spain-mallorca-rape-tourists-british-french-magaluf-71fb9fa0a3c9348e98ebfaa6eb75bae1 (AP)]
*[[United States federal judge]] [[James V. Selna]] rejects a proposed [[United States dollar|$]]200 million settlement in a [[class action|class-action lawsuit]] prompted by a rise in thefts of vehicles manufactured by [[South Korea|South Korean]] automakers [[Hyundai Motor Company|Hyundai]] and [[Kia]]. [https://apnews.com/article/hyundai-kia-settlement-tentative-rejection-f1ad760620101c55ac3b5cf934aab298 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*Aftermath of the [[2023 Thai general election]]
**The [[Constitutional Court of Thailand]] dismisses the petitions on election winner [[Pita Limjaroenrat]]'s renomination as [[Prime Minister of Thailand|prime minister]], allowing a new round of leadership elections in the [[National Assembly (Thailand)|National Assembly]] to take place. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2023/08/17/world/asia-oceania/thai-court-junks-case-on-pitas-failed-pm-bid/1905681 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]
*[[Vanuatu]] [[Prime Minister of Vanuatu|Prime Minister]] [[Ishmael Kalsakau]] survives a [[no-confidence vote]], with the opposition falling one vote short of removing him from power. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/vanuatu-prime-minister-face-no-confidence-vote-parliament-2023-08-16/ (Reuters)]
*The [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] unanimously votes for expulsion of [[Negros Oriental]] representative [[Arnolfo Teves Jr.]] due to his continued absence. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/news/08/16/23/house-expels-teves-over-abandonment-of-office (ABS-CBN News)]
*The [[Central American University (Managua)|Central American University]] in [[Managua]], [[Nicaragua]], suspends its operations after the [[Government of Nicaragua|government]] seizes its assets, alleging the university's involvement in [[terrorism]] during the [[2018 Nicaraguan protests|2018 protests]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20230817-nicaragua-seizes-jesuit-university (AFP via RFI)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Luna programme]]
**[[Roscosmos]] spacecraft [[Luna 25]] enters into a [[lunar orbit]] around the [[Moon]] as it prepares to make a soft landing on the [[lunar south pole]] in the coming days. [https://www.reuters.com/technology/space/russias-luna-25-spacecraft-enters-lunar-orbit-space-agency-2023-08-16/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup]]
**The current [[UEFA Women's Euro 2022|European champions]] [[England women's national football team|England]] advance to the [[FIFA Women's World Cup]] [[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup final|final]] for the first time after defeating co-host [[Australia women's national soccer team|Australia]] 3–1 in the [[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup knockout stage#Australia vs England|semi-final]]. They will play against fellow first-time finalists [[Spain women's national football team|Spain]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/sport/live-news/australia-england-womens-world-cup-semifinal/index.html (CNN)]
